imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: A Moment Was Not a Repair. Cast/design continuity: Two fictional former friends at a small shop counter: a short-haired man in faded blue work shirt and a woman with tied dark hair in muted rose blouse. A fine dark seam across the worn wooden counter is the only restrained symbol of rupture. Ordinary shop setting; no identifiable assailant or weapon.. CELL 0: Wide shop interior. The two people work on opposite sides of a small counter seam, handing a plain folded cloth across at arms length without meeting eyes. Their shoulders and gazes show guarded distance, hands credibly touching the task and counter. CELL 1: Same shop and counter. The man pauses his work and looks across with regret; the woman turns her head only partway, palm resting flat against her own side of the counter. The seam stays visible between them. No fabricated cause of their rupture is pictured. CELL 2: A subdued warm alarm light falls into the otherwise ordinary shop. Both people bend knees and lower behind the counter, the man offering a practical low guiding hand. Tension is in posture and eyes, not spectacle. No weapon, attacker, collision or invented danger source. CELL 3: Low wide view behind the same counter. Both crouch with balanced bodies, shoes on the floor. Their hands meet across the old counter seam at a credible distance; the woman turns to check his face. Fear creates temporary contact, not a romantic embrace. CELL 4: Alarm light has faded. Both remain seated low behind the counter catching breath, their hands loosely touching but beginning to relax apart. The man looks at the woman with gratitude and unresolved sadness; she listens. The physical seam remains intact. CELL 5: Wide quiet shop after danger. Both stand safely at their own work positions, hands now separate on the counter, a little more aware of each other yet without a reunion embrace. The seam is still visible and no repair, heart symbol or triumphant ending is added. Editorial limit: Shared danger must not imply repaired betrayal. No weapon or invented assailant. Keep final distance humane and unresolved.
